newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's ruling Gaullists back candidate age caps.
newsitem.headline: France's ruling Gaullists back candidate age caps.

text.p: France's governing Gaullists, seeking a more youthful image, favour imposing age limits on future candidates for elected office, party leaders said on Wednesday.

Leaders of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR), answering a plea by 51-year-old Prime Minister Alain Juppe for ways to modernise the party, recommended an age ceiling of 75 on RPR candidates in 1998 elections.
The ceiling would fall to 70 for future polls. Current RPR parliamentarians would not be affected.
The RPR leadership, meeting behind closed doors on Tuesday, had also urged new efforts to increase the number of women candidates standing for the Gaullists, officials said.
They said that at least one third of RPR candidates standing for the European parliament as well as for regional and municipal posts should in future be women.
The party leaders also recommended that RPR members be barred from serving simultaneously in both the French and European parliaments.
